title: A Coulomb ground-state density without Kohn-Sham ensemble representation
main_claim: For D=10^200 and an integer Z given by an exact nonnumerical prescription (Eq. explicit-charge), the 3-electron Coulomb Hamiltonian with charges Z,Z at ±(D/Z)e_z has a normalizable absolute ground state in S_z=1/2 whose density is not the density of any ground-state ensemble of a noninteracting Hamiltonian with a real, spin-independent potential in L^{3/2}+L^∞. A corollary says the ensemble Hxc functional has no full-domain local first variation at that density.

issues.location: Sec. 2, Lemma channel-cutoff and Prop. fixed-parameter-channels (02-channels.tex)
issues.description: The pointwise exterior derivative bounds on the residual R and on the density cutoff error come from weighted H^1(R^9) estimates plus a cluster/parallel-derivative regularity argument (citing FS18). The argument is only sketched. At a fixed non-small coupling t_*, the paper says the constants are allowed to depend on t, which is plausible, but the steps are not written out. This is a completeness concern, not an identified error.
issues.evidence: "Difference quotients followed by these local estimates give any fixed number of x-derivatives of the difference, at size O(lambda) in weighted local norms."

issues.description: The Q-gap c_D is at most d_* (B_0 G = d_* G with G in QK), so it is exponentially small in D. The paper says the relevant constants do not depend on the inverse of d_*, by spin non-cancellation (Eq. spin-noncancellation). I checked that bound, (1-2^{-1/2})(2b^2+|S|^2) <= |bG+S|^2, and it is correct. Constants that depend on c_D are folded into C_D and rho_D(R), which is legitimate because D is fixed first. It is worth flagging only as a delicate point.
issues.evidence: "B>=0, B_Q>=c_D>0 uniformly on the small coupling interval" together with "B_0G=d_*G"

coverage: Read main.tex intro and statement and all of Sections 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 in full. Read most of Section 2: the cutoff equation, the slow-channel expansion, the complementary/plane-coefficient lemma, the uniform three-scale density proof and the fixed-parameter proposition. The cluster-regularity details were only skimmed. Checks made: (1) two-centre IMS constants, d_* <= 1/D+60/D^2 and the even gap 3/8-1/D-60/D^2 > 0.2. (2) Angle minimizer existence, the multiplier rule and d>0. (3) Exterior gap: the integration-by-parts and strip-boundary-cost identity, and the constant (2/pi^2)(1/4-1/100-pi^2/400)=0.04363 (computed). (4) The strip-series bound: sum 20(1+l)^2 10^{2l}/(2l)! = 8.5e6 < 1e8 (computed). (5) The weighted divergence -2k(2/sqrt5) = -1.77 < -1. (6) The quantitative-gap localization (Delta_ev/4 > 0.05, 0.03-10/S^2 > d). (7) The ensemble Pauli certificate d(3-2)=d. (8) Potential identification via Slater-Condon and Kato's representation theorem. (9) Translated potential limits giving W=d+k^2/2, the Agmon bound and the trace divergence exponent p^{2beta-7}. (10) The conjugated radial recursion coefficients: verified with sympy that the r^{-j-1} coefficient is -jk and the r^{-j-2} coefficient is -(beta-j)(beta-j+1)/2. (11) The equatorial coefficient T_4 = -a_0'(0) B_Q^{-2} Q Y_z phi and that it is nonzero. (12) The delta_* derivative-ratio bounds. (13) The Z selection logic: t_*=1/Z is not in B. (14) The corollary's subgradient signs.
